import Mathlib
import Nodes.«spec-23b0fff0».Context

/-- Integrality of the binary tails, the second line of every digit-method proof for Erdős 257
(Erdős 1948 and 1968, Duverney–Tachiya 2019). Write `f_A(m) = #{a ∈ A : a ∣ m}` for the
coefficients of the binary expansion `∑_{a ∈ A} 1/(2^a - 1) = ∑_{m ≥ 1} f_A(m)/2^m`
(`Opn.erdos_257_lambert_identity`) and `T_j = ∑_{i ≥ 1} f_A(j+i)/2^i` for the tail after
position `j`, scaled by `2^j`. If the sum is the rational `p/q` then, for every `j`,
`q · T_j = p · 2^j - q · ∑_{m ≤ j} f_A(m) 2^(j-m)`, an integer. Every proof of a special case
then shows that for a well-chosen `j` this integer cannot exist: it is positive whenever some
element of `A` exceeds `j` (so `T_j ≥ 1/q`), while a block of coefficients `f_A(j+1), …,
f_A(j+k)` that vanish, or are divisible by `2^k`, forces `q · T_{j+k} ≥ 2^k` against an upper
bound on that tail. In Lean `2^(j-m)` is a natural-number power with `m ≤ j`, so the subtraction
is exact, and `f_A(0) = 0` by the guard `0 < m`. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_lambert_tail_integral :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), 0 < q →
    ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1) = p / q →
    ∀ j : ℕ,
      (q : ℝ) * ∑' i : ℕ, (Set.ncard {a ∈ A | a ∣ j + i + 1} : ℝ) / 2 ^ (i + 1) =
        ((p * 2 ^ j -
          q * ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), (Set.ncard {a ∈ A | 0 < m ∧ a ∣ m} : ℤ) * 2 ^ (j - m)
          : ℤ) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

justification.text: The divisor is zero only at n = 0, where Lean's junk value makes the term 0, the convention every node of this target uses.
q is a natural number with the hypothesis 0 < q, so the division is by a positive real.
The divisor 2^(i+1) is a positive real for every natural i.

statement.text:
import Mathlib
import Nodes.«spec-689ac1ac».Context

/-- The divisible-block step of the Chowla–Erdős method for Erdős 257. Write
`f_A(m) = #{a ∈ A : a ∣ m}` for the binary coefficients of `∑_{a ∈ A} 1/(2^a - 1)`
(`Opn.erdos_257_lambert_identity`) and `T_j = ∑_{i ≥ 1} f_A(j+i)/2^i` for the tail after
position `j`. Suppose the sum is the rational `p/q`. If the `k` coefficients after position `y`,
`f_A(y+1), …, f_A(y+k)`, are all divisible by `2^k` (a block of zeros is the case they all
vanish), then `q · T_{y+k}` is an integer multiple of `2^k`. Since `q · T_y` is an integer
(`Opn.erdos_257_lambert_tail_integral`) and `T_y = ∑_{i=1}^k f_A(y+i)/2^i + 2^{-k} T_{y+k}`,
the divisibility makes the finite part an integer too. For infinite `A` the tail `T_{y+k}` is
positive, so the multiple is at least `1` and `q · T_{y+k} ≥ 2^k`: this is the inequality every
Chinese-remainder proof (Erdős 1948 with `f_ℕ = d`, Duverney–Tachiya 2019) contradicts by
choosing `y` so that the tail after the block is small on average. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_divisible_block :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), 0 < q →
    ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1) = p / q →
    ∀ y k : ℕ, (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ k → 2 ^ k ∣ Set.ncard {a ∈ A | a ∣ y + i}) →
      ∃ N : ℤ,
        (q : ℝ) * ∑' i : ℕ, (Set.ncard {a ∈ A | a ∣ y + k + i + 1} : ℝ) / 2 ^ (i + 1) =
          2 ^ k * N := by
  sorry

import Nodes.«spec-689ac1ac».Context

theorem witness : ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (y : ℕ) (k : ℕ),
  (0 : ℕ) < q ∧
    ∑' (n : (↑A : Type)), (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (↑n : ℕ) - (1 : ℝ)) = (↑p : ℝ) / (↑q : ℝ) ∧
      ∀ (i : ℕ), (1 : ℕ) ≤ i → i ≤ k → (2 : ℕ) ^ k ∣ {a : ℕ | a ∈ A ∧ a ∣ y + i}.ncard :=
  ⟨∅, 0, 1, 0, 0, one_pos, by rw [tsum_empty]; simp, fun i h1 h2 => absurd (h1.trans h2) (by norm_num)⟩
